scope: Bounded local zero-credential human takeover, side-effect fencing and governed return-to-Agent slice
implemented: Approval decisions remain operator-issued and are rejected after human takeover
Agent action commits are rejected after human takeover
Agent delivery attempts are rejected after human takeover
New inbound messages are fenced after human takeover
Authenticated, idempotent provider delivery callbacks reconcile committed outbox truth after human takeover
Callback reconciliation does not reopen waits or resume Agent execution for HANDED_OFF Missions
Takeover scope is derived from runtime identity and mismatched caller scope is rejected before mutation
Mission takeover durably projects nonterminal conversation Missions to HANDED_OFF and releases active waits
Return-to-Agent is an explicit governed command, not ordinary resume, and requires the recorded operator, rationale and runtime-derived scope

Return-to-Agent restores each supported sibling Mission from its persisted pre-handoff lifecycle state and wait context before releasing the runtime takeover fence; unreconstructable CREATED/READY handoffs are explicitly rejected
Return-to-Agent is retryable after an interrupted coordinator write because a still-active runtime takeover is accepted as the recovery fence
Mission-scoped return receipts are correlated to the exact trace when available and use a deterministic Mission subject for standalone scheduled Missions
Public lifecycle projections redact operator identity and free-form rationale from return-to-Agent causation IDs while local audit data retains them
Scheduled takeover creates and persists a runtime human-takeover record before the first inbound conversation binding
The first inbound after an unbound scheduled takeover hydrates customer identity without reopening Agent execution

Provider-worker fencing and production-side-effect fencing are not proven.

verification_addenda.scope: Return-to-Agent lifecycle consistency and public-boundary repair
repairs: Restoration now derives the pre-handoff Mission state from the persisted HANDED_OFF lifecycle event and restores every nonterminal sibling Mission sharing the conversation.
Released pre-handoff approval, event and schedule waits are reactivated and projected after the Mission returns through ACTIVE, preserving governed wait context.
Mission restoration is ordered before runtime takeover release; an interrupted operation remains fenced by the active runtime takeover and can be retried without ordinary resume bypass.
Return receipts are Mission-scoped, trace-correlated when possible and deterministic for standalone scheduled Missions without traces.
Public lifecycle causation IDs normalize return-to-Agent commands so operator identity and free-form rationale do not cross the public projection boundary.
Regression coverage now verifies prior approval restoration, standalone scheduled return receipts, sibling Mission restoration and public causation redaction.

verdict: ATLAS-BMR2-P2-004 = IN_PROGRESS / LOCAL_PROVEN — bounded local human takeover, side-effect fencing, authoritative callback reconciliation, retryable governed return-to-Agent restoration, Mission-scoped receipts and public causation redaction are implemented and verified; CI, trusted hosted operator identity, operator-contract harness, hosted/provider-worker fencing, staging, production, billing, commercial and whole-product evidence remain unavailable.
